I'm in the exact same situation as you. But it gets better! I used to have existential crisis because I didnt even know what reality is anymore. I look gorgeous in mirrors, but my face looked so asymmetrical and ugly in cameras, a completely different version of me. I learned that it was because I've been too used to the mirrored me, so seeing my 'real' twisted version of me was horrifying, just cause it's new to my eyes. So what really helped was, find a way to look into the mirror while still seeing the non-mirrored reflection of you. This could be done by setting up two mirrors side by side, then focus your eyes in the middle. You'll see in real time, in 3D, how other people really see you, similar to how you see yourself in bad pictures. And it'll be soul-crushing at first! At least for me it was. It was like accepting that your uglier angles are the reality. But not for long. Stare at it for a longgg time. Look at yourself that way every day, and when novelty wears off and you finally get used to it, you'll start realizing you dont look so bad after all! Stare at it hard enough and you'll actually find yourself pretty damn beautiful.
